key_insight: In this multi-institutional reader study, spectral CT deep learning reconstruction (DLR) generally matched or outperformed hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) for image quality across most body regions and for both conventional and virtual monoenergetic images.
clinical_relevance: If validated in routine practice, DLR could improve spectral CT image quality without sacrificing diagnostic confidence and may support broader use of high-quality reconstructions.
method: Retrospective post hoc analysis of a blinded, multi-reader study of dual-layer spectral CT exams.
Compared HIR (iDose4) versus spectral DLR (Spectral Precise Image) using the same raw data.
Independent radiologist/cardiologist readers scored paired images on a 5-point Likert scale.
evidence_signal: Among 59 CT examinations from 56 patients, DLR was noninferior and often superior to HIR for head, abdomen, and cardiac exams, with statistically significant advantages in several comparisons.
watch_item: Results were based on a selected subset of exams and chest VMI did not show clear noninferiority, so generalization to all protocols and image types should be cautious.
paper_title: Deep Learning Reconstruction versus Hybrid Iterative Reconstruction for Spectral CT: A Multi-Institutional Image Quality Assessment
